newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Nortel to buy 20 percent of Israel's Telr.
newsitem.headline: Nortel to buy 20 percent of Israel's Telr.

text.p: Israel's Koor Industries said on Monday that Canada's Nortel would exercise its option to acquire 20 percent of Koor's Telrad unit for $45 million.

Nortel, formerly Northern Telecom Ltd, will pay $17.5 million in cash and another $27.5 million over four payments carrying interest of Libor +1/8 percent for Telrad Telecommunications and Electronic Industries Ltd.
Nortel's holding will be in newly issued shares and will leave Koor, Israel's biggest holding company, with the remaining 80 percent. Koor also controls Tadiran Ltd, another telecom equipment maker.
Nortel signed the two-year option agreement in January 1995.

Telrad, a closely held manufacturer of telecommunications equipment, had sales of $396 million in 1995. Telrad already has a strategic partnership with Nortel, under which it produces equipment under the Nortel name. It also sells its product independently.
The closing date for the transaction is January 28, 1997, at which time further details of the transaction will be announced, a Koor spokeswoman said.
